Class WhoPasskeyAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.autoconfigure.WhoPasskeyAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration(after=WhoAutoConfiguration.class, afterName="org.springframework.boot.mail.autoconfigure.MailSenderAutoConfiguration") @EnableConfigurationProperties(WhoProperties.class) @ConditionalOnClass(name="org.jwcarman.who.passkey.PasskeyLoginMethod") @ConditionalOnBooleanProperty(name="who.passkey.enabled", matchIfMissing=true) public class WhoPasskeyAutoConfiguration extends Object
Registers passkey beans when who-passkey is on the classpath and the application opts in by setting who.passkey.rp-id.

The provider and the registration guard are built by PasskeyLoginMethod, not published as beans: a lone AuthenticationProvider bean would become Spring Security's global one, and a filter bean would be registered with the servlet container. There is exactly one WebAuthnRelyingPartyOperations bean, since Spring's WebAuthn filters look it up and the provider must verify through the same instance.

    • passkeyLoginMethod

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public PasskeyLoginMethod passkeyLoginMethod(WhoPaths paths, JdbcWhoPasskeyUserRepository userRepository, JdbcWhoPasskeyCredentialRepository credentialRepository, org.springframework.security.web.webauthn.management.WebAuthnRelyingPartyOperations rpOperations, WhoService whoService, WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository sessionRepository, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper> jsonMapper, Clock clock, PasskeySettings settings, WhoEventPublisher whoEventPublisher)
      The provider is built here rather than published as a bean: a lone AuthenticationProvider bean would become Spring Security's global one and switch off the application's UserDetailsService. The login method builds the registration guard.
      Parameters:
      paths - where the passkey endpoints live
      userRepository - who's WebAuthn user entities
      credentialRepository - who's passkey records
      rpOperations - the relying party
      whoService - resolves a passkey to its identity
      sessionRepository - stores the who session a sign-in starts
      jsonMapper - reads WebAuthn requests; a default one when the application has none
      clock - stamps events
      settings - the relying party's settings, for the registration window
      whoEventPublisher - publishes sign-in events
      Returns:
      the login method
